error.message: ValueError: too many values to unpack (expected 3)

blame.author: Sentinel Sandbox <sentinel-sandbox@local>
blame.commit_message: Seed bug: recent_items() slices one extra element, returning n+1 items instead of n

hypothesis.root_cause: recent_items() slices cart.items[-n-1:], which returns n+1 items instead of n (an off-by-one error introduced in commit c2466beff2). Downstream code that unpacks the result expecting exactly n (here, 3) elements fails with "ValueError: too many values to unpack (expected 3)" because it actually receives 4 items.
evidence: Git blame commit message explicitly states: 'Seed bug: recent_items() slices one extra element, returning n+1 items instead of n'
The code `cart.items[-n - 1:]` slices n+1 elements from the end rather than n, confirmed by direct inspection of the line

The error 'too many values to unpack (expected 3)' is consistent with a caller doing something like `a, b, c = recent_items(cart, 3)` and receiving 4 items instead of 3, matching the off-by-one described in the blame
No prior similar incidents in memory, so this is treated as a fresh, isolated seeded bug rather than a recurring pattern
hypothesis.suggested_fix_direction: Change the slice to `cart.items[-n:]` (guarding for n=0 or n > len(cart.items) as needed) so recent_items returns exactly n items, matching callers' unpacking expectations.

fix.commit_message: fix: correct off-by-one slice in recent_items()
fix.summary: recent_items() sliced cart.items[-n-1:], returning n+1 items instead of n and breaking downstream unpacking. Fixed to slice cart.items[-n:] and added a guard for n<=0.
